title: SIU clears Toronto officers in 2013 fatal shooting
article: Toronto Police officers who shot and killed a man more than a year ago in the Sherbourne and Wellesley Sts. area will not face charges, the SIU said Friday.

"I am satisfied that the subject officers acted in the reasonable belief that the lives of their team members and other officers were in imminent peril," Tony Loparco, the director of the province's Special Investigations Unit, said.
The man, who was wanted by police but whose name was never released, pointed what turned out to be a pellet gun at two officers when they attempted to arrest him on Nov. 13, 2013, the SIU said.
The man fired several times towards the officers and the sound suggested it was a cap or pellet gun but there is no indication that information was ever passed on to other officers.
The stand-off continued to another address on the street, with the man "repeatedly" aiming the gun at cops from his position on a rear porch.
Around an hour after cops first approached the man, the Emergency Task Force arrived on scene and a negotiator attempted to speak with the man.
The man arose from his crouched position behind a barricade. He "leaned forward quickly," pointing the gun toward the street and officers positioned there.
"That action and the swift manner in which it occurred caused one of the subject officers to call out that the man had his gun pointed at officers," the SIU statement said.
Two officers shot at the man, who was pronounced dead on scene.
Anyone who saw the gun on scene thought it was real, including a civilian who took cover, Loparco said.
Loparco called it a "mistake that was reasonable in the circumstances."

The SIU investigation involved 15 witness officers, 12 civilian witnesses, and two subject officers as well as video surveillance. One subject officer provided an interview and notes, while the other declined both requests, which is his legal right.
